subject: Invoice routing, deal acceleration, and marketplace checklist for Asteria Labs
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@asteria.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Bastian Cho <bastian@asteria.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement evaluation — marketplace vs direct routes

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the concise call earlier. Procurement asked me to capture 3 things they need before they can recommend a path to Finance:  

1) Invoice ownership and Canopy (our PO system) compatibility — will invoices come from Redwood or from the cloud marketplace seller-of-record?
2) Billing cadence and option for net-45 / net-60 payment terms if we go direct.
3) Whether a private offer / PO can be applied if we list on the marketplace (we prefer the marketplace for faster procurement sign-off, but need private offer flexibility).

Can you send a short checklist that I can forward to procurement (and to Finance) with clear next steps for both marketplace and direct contract flows? Also please include any known timing delta (typical days-to-close).

Appreciate it — Marta

--
Marta Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager, Asteria Labs
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@asteria.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement evaluation — marketplace vs direct routes

Hi Marta,

Thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short checklist below you can drop into your procurement/finance thread. I also attached a one-pager comparing the two flows and a private offer template for your legal/procurement team to review.

Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) — quick summary:
- Seller-of-record: cloud marketplace (cloud bills the customer; Redwood is seller partner).
- Invoice: Cloud provider issues invoice; your PO would target the cloud provider as seller-of-record.
- Payment terms: constrained by marketplace (often net-30); private offers sometimes allow alternative terms but require provider approval.
- Timing: Typically 3–10 business days from PO submission to initial provisioning if PO and buyer/vendor relationship intact.
- Pros: Fast procurement review, easy integration with cloud credits/sponsorships, predictable marketplace SKUs.
- Cons: Less control over invoice custom fields, revenue/cost attribution for internal accounting, limited SLA customizations.

Direct contract (Redwood MSA + PO) — quick summary:
- Seller-of-record: Redwood Inference; we issue invoices directly to Asteria Labs.
- Invoice: Redwood invoice supports custom PO fields, billing contacts, and longer net terms (net-45/net-60 subject to credit approval).
- Payment terms: Negotiable (we can include net-45/60 in private offers or direct SOW).
- Timing: Typical procurement + legal review 5–20 business days depending on redlines and approvals; faster if using pre-approved SOWs or an existing reseller relationship.
- Pros: Full control over invoice fields, easier to map to your internal GL, flexible SLA & data residency commitments.
- Cons: Potentially slower procurement path vs marketplace.

Checklist to forward to Procurement / Finance:  
1) Confirm desired seller-of-record (Marketplace vs Redwood direct).
2) If Marketplace: list preferred cloud provider and whether you will accept provider invoice (include vendor/partner IDs).
3) If direct: confirm billing contact, PO template, desired payment terms (e.g., net-45), and any tax/VAT requirements.
4) For both: include intended start date, expected monthly spend range, and any compliance clauses needed (SOC2, audit logs).
5) Decide whether you want a private offer (we can issue a private offer on marketplace or sign a direct MSA).

Estimated deal velocity (very high level):
- Marketplace (straightforward): 1–2 weeks
- Marketplace + private offer: 2–4 weeks (depends on provider approval)
- Direct contract (standard MSA negotiation): 2–6 weeks

Attachments referenced: redwood_marketplace_vs_direct_onepager.pdf, private_offer_template.docx

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with procurement/finance to walk through. Would Thursday morning PST work?

Best,

Grace O'Connor
Director, Commercial Sales — Redwood Inference

Grace — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Finance/Procurement:  

- Is there a standard invoice XML/EDIFACT or integration your team can provide to ingest invoices into our AR system if we go marketplace? Our AP team prefers machine-readable invoices.
- For direct invoices, what is Redwood's standard payment remittance info and can you add a PO reference field that maps to our Canopy PO ID?
- If we decide marketplace + private offer, what is the approval SLAT from the cloud provider (we need an estimate for the internal project plan)?

If you can reply with short answers we can decide on our side by early next week.

Thanks — Bastian
CTO (acting as project sponsor for procurement flow)
Asteria Labs
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Bastian Cho <bastian@asteria.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@asteria.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice routing, deal acceleration, and marketplace checklist for Asteria Labs

Hi Bastian & Marta — looping in the billing/ops answers below so procurement has a single note to act on.

Short answers:  
- Marketplace invoice formats: Most providers (AWS/Azure/GCP) emit machine-readable invoices (CSV/XML). We have a partner billing spec and can share a sample invoice XML for your AR ingestion. If you need a custom mapping, our finance ops team will work with yours.
- Direct invoice remittance: We will issue Redwood invoices with a dedicated PO reference field. Standard remittance: Redwood Inference, 1200 Market St, Suite 500, San Francisco, CA 94103 — Bank wiring instructions are available on signed SOWs; we can include net-45 terms by request for approved credit.
- Private offer approval SLAT: typical provider review is 3–10 business days after submission (can be shorter for pre-approved partners); edge cases (special pricing or custom terms) may take longer.

Recommended next steps to accelerate:  
1) If you want fastest time-to-provision: request marketplace listing + accept provider invoice, then request a private offer as parallel track if you need longer terms or custom billing fields.
2) If GL mapping or longer terms are blockers: pursue direct Redwood invoice; we can expedite with a short SOW and pre-populated PO template (attached).
3) If you want us to draft the private offer and submit to the provider, reply to this thread and we will start the submission today.

I'll follow up Monday with the sample invoice XML and a short one-page remittance worksheet for your AP team.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
